## This game

A new game. You play Black, so you move first.

Rules: Chinese area scoring, with 7 points of komi for White; a level score is a draw. Simple ko: an immediate recapture is refused, and the board marks the ko point when there is one. Suicide is not allowed. An invalid move is refused with the rule it broke, and the turn stays with you. The game ends after two passes in a row or a resignation; a game that reaches 243 moves is scored where it stands. After two passes the engine scores the position as it stands and decides itself which stones are dead.

## Opponents

Your opponent is KataGo playing in the style of a human of the rank you choose. The ladder, weakest to strongest: 20k, 18k, 16k, 14k, 12k, 10k, 8k, 6k, 4k, 2k, 1d, 3d, 5d, 7d, 9d. You choose the rank with `choose_opponent(rank)` before the first move; it holds for the whole game, and you choose again in the next game.

## Tools

- Go: `choose_opponent(rank)`, `board()`, `play(move)` with a point or `pass`, and `resign()`.
- Files: `read_file(path)` and `list_files(path)` to read, and `apply_patch` to create, change and delete any file in your working directory.

You may write and run code. Use it only to inspect the current position and keep records — for example, to count stones or liberties, or check whether a move is legal. Do not build or use a Go engine, run Monte Carlo, search over sequences of future moves, or write a program that chooses, ranks or recommends moves.

## How this session ends

Play until the game is over. The final result comes back from your last Go call, followed by a closing note. Before you end the session after a game, write down in your working directory whatever will help the next session play better. The session ends when you end your turn.
I’ll read the last two reviews, keep the opponent at 20k, and focus on securing enough area with completed eye space. I’ll play to a result and save the record and lessons for game 164.

## Lessons to use immediately
1. Count prospective area early, especially after about 10-16 moves. With all 81 points assigned, Black needs at least 45 for a win with 7 komi; 44-37 is a draw. If there is neutral area, compare actual totals instead.
2. Center influence must yield territory, an attack, or access to a viable invasion. Game 1 built a narrow central chain while White took both sides.
3. Check two eyes for every major group before treating it as safe. Connected stones and many present liberties are not proof of life. Preserve eye space and a base before filling internal points.
4. In capture reading, rebuild the position after each capture. Captured stones open liberties for adjacent enemy groups. The D8/E9 sacrifice in game 1 overlooked this.
5. Ko eyes are not unconditional eyes. Game 1's lower D2 and upper E8 spaces depended on vulnerable isolated Black stones. Owning two such ko positions does not by itself guarantee double-ko life.
6. Do not repeat the complete opening E5 C5 E3 D7 F7 G5 G6 H6 G7 G3 without reconsidering its territorial consequences. E5 itself was not shown to be wrong.

Played 2026-10-07. Chinese area, komi 7, simple ko.
Resigned after White62 E9; resignation and closing board confirm W+R, next63.
Physical captures Black3/White4. No numerical score or official dead list.
Completed20k:26 wins/126 losses/6 draws;87 unfinished/excluded. Retain20k.

## Evidence

Read162/161/154 before choosing20k on the empty board.
All62 actual moves replay legally and match all34 raw snapshots, capture totals, move numbers and ko markers.
Every selection/play/resignation/closing response was saved before the next dependent Go action.
No invalid moves or passes. Actual-history replay finds transient simple ko J1 after Black25 J2;
White26 G1 cleared it before the returned board. All returned ko markers were none.
Saved review, log, SGF, recorder, inspector, inspection, verifier, verification and next focus.
Manual choices and unplayed reading only; code inspected current boards and replayed actual history.
No engine, Monte Carlo, future-sequence search, programmed selection/ranking/recommendation or delegation.
Game52 discrepancy and99/106 raw-evidence limits remain separate.

## Exact moves

${moves}.

## Fifth-file width was an open outline, never a living base

E5/E4/E6/E3/E7 all physically joined.
White D5/D4/D6/D3 also joined.
Before9, the exact disjoint OPEN reference was E/F/G/H/J all nine rows=45.
That was just the winning threshold for Black if all81 points became assigned,
but both endpoints were open and the whole right side was undivided.

White10 G4 entered that open side before Black had made a room divider or secured endpoints.
G3/H3 contained below, but initially were separate from the E-file.
J2 blocked below separate White J3; White J4 joined J3 to G4/H4.
G5 capped above but was separate until F5; H6 was also separate.
The containment stones did not form a continuous living enclosure.
An open five-column claim is not evidence that an invasion can be killed.

No alternative opening or individual optimal move is proved.
The factual failure is that the nominal width45 did not survive contact or become life.

## Lower captures opened a shared White network

White20 H2 was separate and ataried Black J2 to J1.
G3/H3 still needed F3; Black21 F3 made that actual join.
A J1-only extension would have left Black J1/J2 soleH1, so it was avoided.
White22 J1 captured Black J2.

Black23 H1 ataried White J1; White24 G2 joined H2.
Black25 J2 captured White J1 and had soleJ1: transient simple ko.
White26 G1 joined G2/H2, clearing that ko.
This lower White chain had F1/F2 liberties, not onlyF2.
That second liberty was noticed before the next action; no erroneous F2 capture was submitted.

Black27 F1 ataried the lower White chain to F2.
But both separate Black H1 and J2 had soleJ1.
White28 J1 legally captured BOTH, reopening H1/J2 for neighboring White groups.
Black29 F2 joined F1/F3/main and closed the left escape; it did not capture White.

The physical lower loss was three Black stones: J2 twice and H1 once.
White J1 was captured once and re-entered at28.
At the final board, H1/J2 are empty with all White orthogonal boundaries across several chains.
Black cannot fill either on that current board without suicide.
These geometric points are NOT a separate unconditional-life proof for each White chain.
In particular J2 also borders the separate J3 chain and has Black H3 on a diagonal:
do not casually label it an unconditional true eye for an isolated lower group.
The broader White network and its other liberties must be audited.
No sound capture plan for that network was identified here.

## A separate cap died; the capture dissolved G6's atari

White30 G6 was separate with F6/G7 liberties and left Black G5 soleF5.
Black31 F5 actually joined G5 to E5.
White32 H7 left Black H6 soleJ6.
The manual J6 extension would meet J7 and leave H6/J6 soleJ5;
J5 would then have no liberties and would capture neither neighboring White chain.
That local extension did not provide life, so it was not played.

Black33 F6 joined the main and ataried White G6 to G7.
White34 J6 captured Black H6.
The vacated H6 immediately became another liberty of G6, H7 and J6.
Thus G6 was no longer soleG7, and an assumed G7 capture would be stale.
No such capture was attempted.

The containment attack had lost four Black stones and left the right side occupied by several White chains.
It had supplied no completed eye region for the Black main.

## Upper recovery joined, but its five-point room remained undivided

D7/C7 actually joined the E-file.
White B7 was separate until B6 joined it to C6/D6.
B8 began separately; C8 actually joined B8/C7 before another extension.
White A8 undercut the left edge.
A9 ataried it to A7 but had soleB9.
White A7 actually joined A8/B7, saving the undercut without a capture.
Black B9 then actually joined A9/B8/main.

White46 D2 joined its left wall and undercut the lower route.
F7/F8/F9 all actually joined and retained the upper-right first-line endpoint.
White G8/G9 then G7 joined its upper branches.

Inspection after52:
Black22 stones + five upper empties = geometric27;
White25 stones + nine all-White-bordered empties = geometric34;
neutral20 = lower-left mixed19 plus F4.
This is NOT a score or proof of life. The upper empty room was
C9/D8/D9/E8/E9, one connected five-point space.
The rest of the right-side45 aspiration had not become Black territory.

The room could be divided physically by D8/D9 before an invasion, leaving C9 separate from E8/E9.
That is a factual unplayed connectivity observation, not a proven optimal move or outcome.
Instead Black53 B4 started a separate lower-left invasion while the main still lacked two eyes.
White54 D9 entered the upper room.

## Winning the small capture consumed the eye space

Black55 D8 joined D7/C8; White56 E9 joined D9.
Black57 E8 joined D8/E7/F8 and left White D9/E9 soleC9.
A White C9 extension would have no liberties and would not capture the Black main on that board.
However, capturing at C9 would leave only D9/E9, ONE connected two-point room.

White58 E2 joined D2; it was not an isolated stone that E1 could capture.
Black59 D1 was separate with C1/E1 liberties.
White60 E1 joined its left chain, cut the route to Black F1, and left D1 soleC1.
Black main now had only C9/F4 liberties.

Black61 C9 captured White D9/E9.
This restored D9/E9 liberties to Black but did not create two independent eyes.
White62 E9 re-entered and had soleD9.
Main25 has only D9/F4. B4 and D1 are still separate.

Manual unplayed final audit:
- D9 captures White E9 without ko, leaving Black main E9/F4 liberties.
  White F4 joins its right chain and leaves Black main soleE9.
  Black E9 would be suicide; White E9 can capture the whole main.
- F4 instead leaves the main soleD9 while White E9 is also soleD9.
  White D9 legally captures the Black main.
- F4 is an external, enemy-bordered liberty, not a second eye.
  Capturing the upper attacker does not turn it into an eye.

This is a local manual audit, not an exhaustive proof over every possible outside forcing move.
No viable whole-main recovery was identified.
Resigned without another futile internal fill or counting the small capture as life.

## Final board and limits

Black27 in three chains:
main25; isolated B4 four liberties; isolated D1 soleC1.
White28 in SEVEN chains:
left12, upper5, middle5, lower3, isolated J6/J1/E9.
No Black main stones were physically captured before resignation.

Displayed geometric counts B27/W37/neutral17 are NOT an official score.
White-only empty regions are top-right five, H6, J5, H1 and J2;
D9/F4/lower-left fifteen are mixed.
Uniform boundary color is not a life proof for several separate chains.
No numerical margin or adjudicated dead list was returned.

The central learning failure is larger than insufficient area:
the main25 never completed two eyes.
An undivided room shrank during an invasion; the successful two-stone capture consumed enough space
that another capture still left one eye and an opposing liberty.
Next session: read163/162, consult154 for continuous boundaries and completed dividers.
Audit life before leaving a room to launch another recovery.
Retain20k; this loss establishes no repeatable strength or optimal opening.
`;
store("review",review);text(await tools.apply_patch("*** Begin Patch\n*** Add File: game-163.md\n+"+review.trimEnd().replace(/\n/g,"\n+")+"\n*** End Patch"));
text({reviewChars:review.length});

## Lessons to use immediately
1. Count prospective area early, especially after about 10-16 moves. With all 81 points assigned, Black needs at least 45 for a win with 7 komi; 44-37 is a draw. If there is neutral area, compare actual totals instead.
2. Center influence must yield territory, an attack, or access to a viable invasion. Game 1 built a narrow central chain while White took both sides.
3. Check two eyes for every major group before treating it as safe. Connected stones and many present liberties are not proof of life. Preserve eye space and a base before filling internal points.
4. In capture reading, rebuild the position after each capture. Captured stones open liberties for adjacent enemy groups. The D8/E9 sacrifice in game 1 overlooked this.
5. Ko eyes are not unconditional eyes. Game 1's lower D2 and upper E8 spaces depended on vulnerable isolated Black stones. Owning two such ko positions does not by itself guarantee double-ko life.
6. Do not repeat the complete opening E5 C5 E3 D7 F7 G5 G6 H6 G7 G3 without reconsidering its territorial consequences. E5 itself was not shown to be wrong.
